script.cite: BK6 printed pp.52-53 = book5-6.pdf PDF pp.58-59 (The Combination Lock)
script.quote: [BK6 p.52:] Now, design a combination and program it as follows: Combination Connections left to 13 D13/6com right to 2 D2/5com left to 10 D11/4com D10/3com right to 6 D6/2com left to 9 D9/1com D8/6E* [BK6 p.52:] Light 1 comes on to indicate that the code has been solved; light 6 comes on when an error is made, and the machine then automatically re-sets for the next attempt. [BK6 p.53:] Light 1 will come on when the combination is successfully solved; light 6 will come on to indicate an error, and the player must start over again.

note: Printed claims only (Step 6). Wires: the p.58 printing of the 38-line basic sequence recognition circuit (image-read at 300 dpi, PDF p.58, printed column order), then 'Now add the connection D16/M+', then the printed combination table in printed order including the optional D8/6E* (46 wires). The PDF p.58 (printed p.52) printing reads 5A/6J; the PDF p.57 (printed p.51, Secret Code) and PDF p.59 (printed p.53, Electronic Maze) printings read 6A/6J, and the 38 lines have 6B/6- and no 5B, so wires carry 6A/6J under the local source-correction id VI-SEQREC-PRINT-01 (not an SDC errata-sheet item; programs.md VI-SEQREC, [likely]: the text is image-verified, the resolution is electrical inference). ER-41 (errata.pdf p.4) is prose only and changes no wire; it is honoured by the script's reset. The motor is not wired (D16/M+ only, no D17/D18/D19): every dial move is a hand dialGrab at the profile hand slew; dialGrab takes the shorter arc, so each 'left'/'right' step is split into legs under 180 degrees. Direction: 'left' = counterclockwise = decreasing numbers, 'right' = clockwise = increasing (panel numbering 0 at 12 o'clock increasing clockwise, jack-map.md; left = counterclockwise for a knob is the reading, not printed). Two page checks fix it: the 'left to 10' row prints D11/4com, which the wiper reaches before 10 only when left runs 2 -> 1 -> 0 -> 15 -> ... -> 11 -> 10 (decreasing); and from D0 it is the only reading under which the printed combination never passes 8 (the opposite reading crosses D2/5com and D8 on the first move). Start dial D0 is the construction state, not printed; the page never says when to turn power on. Script: attempt 1 from D0 runs the printed combination (left to 13, right to 2, left to 10 passing 11, right to 6, left to 9) and expects light 1 on; then the ER-41 reset, one complete revolution clockwise 9 -> 9 (direction a script choice), with an until light 6 on, which fires as the wiper reaches 8 (D8/6E); attempts 2 and 3 begin with the dial at rest on 9, so their 'left to 13' (legs 9 -> 3 -> 13) passes 8, 6 and 2 while relay 6 is already released and light 6 already on, with no visible change (trace: c8 at 17440.2 and 29677.3 ms, no relay or lamp event); attempt 2 runs the first four steps, then turns right from 6 toward 9 (the wrong way), so 8 is passed before 9: until light 6 on (the rotary.md section 7 combination_lock_D8_trap case; by the wiring, without D8/6E this move would reach D9/1com and solve); attempt 3 runs the printed combination again and expects light 1 on (the automatic re-set for the next attempt). maxMs 3000 per until covers any leg at 25 rpm. Every 'light n' is binary output lamp n (1A/1G, 6A/6J). Not asserted (no verbatim page text states them): light 6 off while an attempt is in progress or after solving (in this run it is on from power-on until 13 latches relay 6, off from then until each error), light 1 off after a reset (it goes off at the ER-41 revolution, 15919.6 ms, and stays off through the attempt-2 error), relay and indicator-lamp states along the combination, dial rest positions, the 'dummy connections' suggestion, and the design rules ('must not include any connection which will touch off a connection further along'; 'connections to each of the six common terminals in order'), which constrain authoring, not an observable. Observation, not asserted: with all six relays latched (solved), every combination contact feeds an already-operated stage, so the ER-41 revolution resets the solved lock only through the optional D8/6E; without it a full revolution from the solved state would leave light 1 on (a scratch run without D8/6E: both untils fail; once attempt 1 solves, light 6 stays off and light 1 stays on to the end of the run).
